Alano]] |blank1_name = Political party |blank1_info = {{Color box|{{Party color|Partido Federal ng Pilipinas}}|border=darkgray}} [[Partido Federal ng Pilipinas|PFP]] |blank2_name = Congressional bloc |blank2_info = Majority }} '''Basilan's at-large congressional district''' refers to the lone [[congressional district of the Philippines]] in the province of [[Basilan]]. The province has been represented in the country's [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|national legislatures]] since 1984.{{cite web |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=March 8, 2021 |archive-date=March 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316064243/http://congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |url-status=dead }} It first elected a representative provincewide [[at-large]] during the [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election]] following the restoration of provincial and city district representation in the [[Batasang Pambansa]] where Basilan had previously been included in the regionwide representation of [[Western Mindanao]] (Region IX) for the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa|interim parliament]].{{cite web|url=http://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l82d3 |title=Batas Pambansa Blg. 660, (1984-03-07) |publisher=Lawyerly |accessdate=March 8, 2021}} The province, created by the 1973 separation from [[Zamboanga del Sur]] of the entire island with its two municipal districts and the municipality of [[Isabela, Basilan|Isabela]] outside its [[poblacion]] which was earlier organized as the City of Basilan separated from [[Zamboanga City]], was formerly represented as part of [[Zamboanga del Sur's at-large congressional district|Zamboanga del Sur's]], [[Zamboanga's at-large congressional district|Zamboanga's]] and [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]]'s at-large representations in earlier legislatures.{{cite web|url=https://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1948/ra_288_1948.html |title=Republic Act No. 288 |publisher=Arellano Law Foundation |accessdate=March 8, 2021}}{{cite web|url=https://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l2dbf |title=Republic Act No. 711, (1952-06-06) |publisher=Lawyerly |accessdate=March 8, 2021}}{{cite web|url=https://lawphil.net/statutes/presdecs/pd1973/pd_356_1973.html |title=Presidential Decree No. 356 |publisher=Arellano Law Foundation |accessdate=March 8, 2021}}{{cite web|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1975/12/11/presidential-decree-no-840-s-1975/ |title=Presidential Decree No. 840, s. 1975 |date=11 December 1975 |publisher=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)]] |accessdate=March 8, 2021}} Since the 1987 restoration of Congress following the ratification of a new constitution, Basilan has been entitled to one member in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]].{{cite web|url=https://www.chanrobles.com/ordinance.htm |title=The 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines |publisher=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |accessdate=March 8, 2021}} It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Yusop Alano|Yusop T. Alano]] of the [[Partido Federal ng Pilipinas]] (PFP).{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |access-date=March 8, 2021}} ==Representation history== {| class=wikitable |- ! rowspan="2" | # ! rowspan="2" colspan=2 | Image ! rowspan="2" | Member ! colspan=2 | Term of office ! rowspan="2" | Batasang
